summary.text: 机 was recorded with a wood-related meaning and analyzed as 木, the meaning component, plus 几, the sound component. It later came to write 機, the graph for “mechanism,” through a proposed borrowing based on similar sound; the old tree name and its pronunciation remain unverified. (ref003, ref022, ref035)

formation.text: The historical analysis treats 机 as a phonosemantic compound: 木 marks a wood-related category, while 几 supplies sound. This describes the graph recorded for the wood-related sense, not how 机 later came to stand for 機. (ref003, ref035)

components.text: 木 marks the wood-related category in the historical analysis. The old gloss does not identify a particular tree. (ref003, ref029, ref035)
几 is identified as the sound component in the historical analysis of 机. A reading is reported for the graph, but it does not establish how the tree word was pronounced. (ref003, ref032, ref035)

sound_limitation.text: The reported historical reading belongs to the graph 机; the evidence does not establish it as the pronunciation of the tree word or provide an independent comparison for that word.

history.text: The selected image shows 機 in small-seal style as a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact. It illustrates the graph’s recorded analysis as 木 plus sound-bearing 幾. (ref028, ref034)

The historical account records 机 and 機 as separate graphs, with different components and fanqie readings. It describes later use of 机 to write 機 because of similar sound; that established substitution became the simplified form used in mainland China. Its first dated occurrence is unresolved. (ref022, ref035)

A phonological dataset gives both graphs the Mandarin reading jī, while reporting distinct Middle Chinese and Old Chinese forms. The 机 row is local dataset evidence; the upstream source was not independently verified for that row. (ref032, ref037)

uncertainties.text: The old tree referent and its spoken name are not established. The graph’s reconstructed reading alone cannot prove the tree word’s pronunciation or demonstrate the proposed sound basis for borrowing 机 to write 機. (ref032, ref035)

The evidence does not establish oracle-bone or bronze forms, a graphic corruption sequence, or the development from earlier forms to the present graphs. The selected seal-style image is a modern redraw. (ref026, ref034)
The first dated use of 机 for 機 remains unresolved. (ref022, ref035)

senses.text: The historical dictionary glosses 机 as 木也 and analyzes it with 木 and sound-bearing 几. This is the earliest sense supported here, though it does not identify the tree or date an inscription bearing this meaning. (ref003, ref029, ref035)
A phonological dataset associates 机 with the gloss “small table, stool.” Its date and relation to the wood-related sense are unresolved. (ref032, ref037)

机 is listed with the meaning “desk” or “table” in modern Chinese and Japanese reference data. A chronological path from the older wood-related or small-table senses is not established. (ref005, ref008)

In mainland simplified writing, 机 is used for the mechanism word written 機 in the traditional graph. This is described as sound-based reuse of a graph, not a meaning change from wood or table; the old tree name and sound are unverified. (ref022, ref035, ref016)
“Moment” appears among the definitions for 机, but its chronology and whether it belongs to the graph’s independent sense history or its later use for 機 are unresolved. (ref005, ref016, ref035)

developments.text: Both meanings are associated with 机, but no chronology or semantic link between them is established. (ref003, ref032)

The account describes later writers reusing 机 to write 機 because the words were thought to sound alike. This is borrowing the written sign for a different word, not a shift from “wood” to “mechanism.” Since the old tree name and pronunciation are unknown, the sound match remains proposed rather than demonstrated. (ref022, ref032, ref035)

limitations.text: The earliest date for the wood-related gloss, the tree referent, and its spoken name are not established. (ref029, ref033, ref035)
The reported meanings do not establish a secure chronology or connected semantic path among the wood-related, table, desk, and moment senses. (ref005, ref008, ref032, ref037)

overview.text: 机 was recorded for a wood-related meaning, with 木 marking the category and 几 supplying sound. It later came to write 機, “mechanism,” through a proposed borrowing based on similar sound; the old tree name and its pronunciation are unverified. (ref003, ref022, ref035)

components.text: 木 marks the wood-related category; the particular tree is not identified. (ref003, ref029)
几 is named as the sound component, but its reported reading does not establish the old tree word’s pronunciation. (ref003, ref032, ref035)

takeaway.text: The meaning “mechanism” comes from reusing 机 to write 機 based on a proposed sound similarity, not from a demonstrated change in meaning. (ref022, ref035)

relationships.text: The historical analysis identifies 木 as the meaning component in 机. (ref003, ref035)
The historical analysis identifies 几 as supplying sound in 机. (ref003, ref029)
